name: Dusk Hypothetical
niche: Second-person 'what if' hypotheticals: everyday superpowers, strange rules of the world, and what would really happen, with one real-world fact per beat
audience: English-speaking teens and young adults (13-25) who like curious, slightly funny thought experiments, long enough to unfold in chapters
title_rules: Start with 'What If'; second person; under 60 characters; one concrete hook (a number, a power, a rule)
thumbnail_rules: One big sphere-headed figure close-up with a strong eye expression; 2-3 word gold caps text that adds to the title; violet dusk background

decisions.text: Narration is second person, present tense, short sentences (5-8 words), fast steady pace; one real-world fact card per escalation beat; never copy the reference channel's structure (no mid-triumph cold open, no life-or-death binary climax)
Default length is about 10 minutes (the measured reference set runs 10.5 min). Structure it in chapters with a short chapter card each.

Long films need rising stakes that are not life-or-death: a deadline or loss set up in the first minute, each chapter closer to it, every beat bigger than the last, an open question about every 90 s. Add short side-character lines (another voice or a speech bubble).
Grade to the style's measured look: median luma about 0.26 (range 0.20-0.30), saturation about 0.35; keep night and mood-flood shots readable; master loudness range 2.5-3 LU, first word at 0 s.

2026-11-13: replaces the 'never copy the reference structure' rule. Follow the reference channel's script structure and pacing (opening, escalation, climax, ending, chapter rhythm, minute by minute); stories, lines, characters, voice, names and thumbnails stay our own.
